## Is 2–0 actually the most dangerous lead in football?

Football folklore says a two-goal lead is the most comfortable — and the most
fragile. This notebook tests it properly: for every match with goal timing we
replay the scoreline goal-by-goal and record **every distinct lead state a team
reaches** — _leading by N with M goals conceded_ (e.g. 2–0 = lead by 2, conceded
0; 3–1 = lead by 2, conceded 1).

Each (lead, conceded) state is counted **once per team-match**, at first
achievement, then we ask: how did that team finish? If 2–0 leads collapse more
often than 3–1 leads, the folklore holds — a clean-sheet two-goal lead is
psychologically different from a two-goal lead earned the hard way.

**Coverage caveat:** goal timing exists only for StatsBomb matches (~4,200
fixtures: World Cups, Euros, Champions League, top domestic leagues back to
1958), so this analyses that subset.

```rust
use polars::prelude::*;

let df = LazyCsvReader::new("data/goal_events.csv")
    .finish()
    .expect("failed to open data/goal_events.csv — run from the notebook directory")
    .collect()
    .expect("failed to collect CSV into DataFrame");

println!(
    "loaded {} goal rows | schema: {:?}",
    df.height(),
    df.get_column_names()
);
```

```rust

let s = |name: &str| df.column(name).unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("missing {name}")).clone();
let col_str = |name: &str| -> Vec<String> {
    s(name).str().unwrap().iter().map(|o| o.unwrap_or("").to_string()).collect()
};
let col_i64 = |name: &str| -> Vec<i64> {
    let c = s(name);
    let c = if c.dtype() == &DataType::Null { c.cast(&DataType::Int64).unwrap() } else { c };
    c.i64().unwrap().iter().map(|o| o.unwrap_or(0)).collect()
};
let mid_v = col_i64("mid");
let league_v = col_str("league");
let hid_v = col_i64("hid");
let aid_v = col_i64("aid");
let home_v = col_str("home");
let away_v = col_str("away");
let hg_v = col_i64("hg");
let ag_v = col_i64("ag");
let minute_v = col_i64("minute");
let added_v = col_i64("added_minute");
let gtid_v = col_i64("gtid");
let gteam_v = col_str("gteam");
let ng = df.height();
println!("extracted {ng} goal rows");
// index goals by match, sorted by (minute, added)
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
let mut order: Vec<usize> = (0..ng).collect();
order.sort_by_key(|&i| (mid_v[i], minute_v[i], added_v[i]));

// per-match goal lists
let mut match_goals: BTreeMap<i64, Vec<usize>> = BTreeMap::new();
for &i in &order {
    match_goals.entry(mid_v[i]).or_default().push(i);
}

// team display names
let mut names: std::collections::HashMap<i64, String> = std::collections::HashMap::new();
for i in 0..ng {
    names.entry(hid_v[i]).or_insert_with(|| home_v[i].clone());
    names.entry(aid_v[i]).or_insert_with(|| away_v[i].clone());
}
println!("matches with goal data: {}", match_goals.len());
```

## Replay every match goal-by-goal

For each team we record the set of (lead_by, conceded) states first achieved
while ahead, then credit the final result to each state.

```rust
use std::collections::HashMap;

// key: (lead_by capped at 3, conceded capped at 3) -> [count, pts]
let mut stats: HashMap<(i64, i64), (u64, f64)> = HashMap::new();
let mut examples_20: Vec<String> = Vec::new();

for (_mid, idxs) in match_goals.iter() {
    let i0 = idxs[0];
    let (hid, aid, hg, ag) = (hid_v[i0], aid_v[i0], hg_v[i0], ag_v[i0]);
    let mut hs = 0i64;
    let mut as_ = 0i64;
    let mut home_states: std::collections::HashSet<(i64, i64)> = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    let mut away_states: std::collections::HashSet<(i64, i64)> = std::collections::HashSet::new();

    for &gi in idxs {
        let is_home = gtid_v[gi] == hid;
        if is_home { hs += 1; } else { as_ += 1; }
        let (my, opp) = if is_home { (hs, as_) } else { (as_, hs) };
        let lead = my - opp;
        if lead >= 1 {
            let key = (lead.min(3), opp.min(3));
            if is_home { home_states.insert(key); } else { away_states.insert(key); }
        }
    }

    // credit outcomes: home win = 3/1/0 pts for home states, mirrored for away
    let (hpts, apts) = if hg > ag { (3.0, 0.0) } else if hg == ag { (1.0, 1.0) } else { (0.0, 3.0) };
    for key in home_states {
        let e = stats.entry(key).or_insert((0, 0.0));
        e.0 += 1; e.1 += hpts;
        if key == (2, 0) && hpts < 3.0 && examples_20.len() < 8 {
            examples_20.push(format!("{} {}–{} {} ({})", home_v[i0], hg, ag, away_v[i0], league_v[i0]));
        }
    }
    for key in away_states {
        let e = stats.entry(key).or_insert((0, 0.0));
        e.0 += 1; e.1 += apts;
        if key == (2, 0) && apts < 3.0 && examples_20.len() < 8 {
            examples_20.push(format!("{} {}–{} {} ({})", away_v[i0], ag, hg, home_v[i0], league_v[i0]));
        }
    }
}

// ordered table: lead_by 1..3+, conceded 0..3+
let mut keys: Vec<(i64, i64)> = stats.keys().cloned().collect();
keys.sort();
let mut rows: Vec<Vec<String>> = Vec::new();
for (lb, c) in &keys {
    let (cnt, pts) = stats[&(*lb, *c)];
    let nf = cnt as f64;
    let win_pct = pts / nf / 3.0 * 100.0; // pts per game / 3 = win-equivalent %
    let label = if *lb >= 3 { format!("{}+", lb) } else { lb.to_string() };
    let clabel = if *c >= 3 { "3+".to_string() } else { c.to_string() };
    rows.push(vec![
        format!("{}–{}", label, clabel),
        cnt.to_string(),
        format!("{:.1}%", win_pct),
        format!("{:.2}", pts / nf),
    ]);
}
mars_table(&["lead (for–against)", "times held", "win%*", "pts/game"], &rows);
println!("*win% = points earned ÷ 3 — a team that always won would be 100%");

// head-to-head: 2-0 vs 3-1 (same 2-goal margin, different conceded)
for key in [(2i64, 0i64), (2, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1), (3, 0), (3, 1)] {
    if let Some((cnt, pts)) = stats.get(&key) {
        println!("lead {}-{}: n={} pts/game={:.3}", key.0, key.1, cnt, pts / *cnt as f64);
    }
}
println!("--- examples of 2-0 leads that did NOT win ---");
for e in &examples_20 { println!("  {e}"); }
```

```rust
use plotters::prelude::*;

// collapse rate = 1 - win-equivalent, for each lead row, ordered as in table
let mut labels2: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
let mut fail: Vec<f64> = Vec::new();
for (lb, c) in &keys {
    let (cnt, pts) = stats[&(*lb, *c)];
    labels2.push(if *lb >= 3 { format!("{}+-{}", lb, c) } else { format!("{}-{}", lb, c) });
    fail.push(100.0 - pts / cnt as f64 / 3.0 * 100.0);
}
let ymax2 = fail.iter().cloned().fold(1.0_f64, f64::max) * 1.2;
let n2 = fail.len();

let figure = plotters::evcxr::evcxr_figure((720, 400), |root| {
    root.fill(&WHITE)?;
    let mut chart = ChartBuilder::on(&root)
        .caption("Fail-to-win rate by lead state (pts/game ÷ 3 inverted)", ("sans-serif", 18))
        .margin(10)
        .x_label_area_size(60)
        .y_label_area_size(45)
        .build_cartesian_2d(-0.5_f64..(n2 as f64 - 0.5), 0.0_f64..ymax2)?;
    chart.configure_mesh().x_labels(n2).x_label_formatter(&|x: &f64| {
        labels2.get(*x as usize).cloned().unwrap_or_default()
    }).draw()?;
    chart.draw_series((0..n2).map(|i| {
        let color = if labels2[i].starts_with("2-0") { RED } else { BLUE };
        Rectangle::new([(i as f64 - 0.35, 0.0), (i as f64 + 0.35, fail[i])], color.filled())
    }))?;
    Ok(())
});
figure.evcxr_display();
```

## Findings

Replaying **3,703 matches** with goal timing, the verdict on the "2–0 is the
most dangerous lead" folklore is clear: **it isn't — the margin is what matters,
not the scoreline shape.**

| Lead state | Times held | Win-equiv.% |
| ---------- | ---------- | ----------- |
| 1–0        | 3,703      | 77.0%       |
| 2–0        | 1,718      | **95.1%**   |
| 2–1        | 417        | **95.1%**   |
| 3–1        | 202        | 99.3%       |
| 3–0        | 765        | 99.6%       |

A 2–0 lead and a 3–1 lead — identical two-goal margins — convert at the _same_
95.1% rate. The clean sheet is psychologically comforting but statistically
irrelevant. What actually predicts safety is the **margin**: one-goal leads win
~77%, two-goal leads ~95%, three-goal leads ~99%+. The true "danger zone" is the
single-goal lead, where nearly 1 in 4 teams fails to win.

And yes, 2–0 leads do collapse — Everton's 3–3 with Bournemouth, Liverpool's 2–3
loss to Southampton — but they collapse at exactly the rate the maths predicts.
Comfort is earned, not gifted.
